text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm starting the onboarding for atlas-13b (v1). Putting this thread as the single place for weights location, tokenizer oddities, and access checks.

jonathan: thanks — do we have the HF origin URL?

maria: yes: https://huggingface.co/org/atlas-13b/tree/main. We mirrored the weights to s3://redwood-registry/models/atlas-13b/v1/ earlier today.

lee: pinging svc-artifacts for write access — CI will need to fetch shards during the build. Who owns the iam role?

ashley: svc-artifacts is under infra/team-keys, role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/svc-artifacts. I can add the model-registry CI role if you list the exact principal.

maria: CI principal is arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-model-registry. If infra can grant s3:GetObject to that role for s3://redwood-registry/models/atlas-13b/v1/* that should be enough for the smoke ingest.

jonathan: also flagged a tokenizer mismatch in the manifest — tokenizer.json says sentencepiece, but the repo has a legacy spiece.model built with a different pad id. Sophie — can you verify tokenization?

sophie: looked quickly — vocab and merges absent, so it is a sentencepiece model, but pad_id in tokenizer.json is 0 while the spiece.model expects 1. That causes decode errors in local eval.

maria: ugh. So either update tokenizer.json pad_token_id to 1 or regenerate spiece.model with pad=0. Which is less risky?

lee: updating tokenizer.json is safer for now (less binary churn). But we should add a CI check to validate tokenizer roundtrip.

ashley: agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to patch tokenizer.json to pad_token_id: 1 and add a unit that runs tokenizer.encode/decode on a few samples. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry/pull/4567 :eyes:

maria: thanks — can someone also sanity-check checksums for the shards? I ran sha256 on one file:

```
sha256sum weights-00001.bin
# output: 2f7c9b1a3d0e4a6b9e8b6f3d2c5a1e4b9c7d6e5f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2
```

jonathan: good to include manifest field checksum_sha256. Add to manifest.json: 
```
{
  "shards": [
    {"path": "weights-00001.bin", "sha256": "2f7c9b1a3d0e4a6b9e8b6f3d2c5a1e4b9c7d6e5f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2"}
  ]
}
```
ingest-bot: deploy-bot presign request accepted for 1h TTL. Presigned URL: https://presign.redwood.internal/s/atlas-13b/v1/weights-00001.bin?X-Amz-Expires=3600

maria: perfect. I'll kick off the ingest job on the staging registry with that URL.

lee: quick checklist for finalizing:
- patch tokenizer.json (ashley)
- add manifest checksums (maria/jonathan)
- grant s3:GetObject to ci-model-registry if not already (ashley)
- add tokenizer roundtrip test in CI (ashley)
- run full smoke ingest and sample inference on staging (maria)

sophie: small note — ensure equals_ignore_case normalization for added tokenizer tests; the tokenizer lowercasing behavior is slightly different between hf and our runtime.

maria: noted — will include lowercase test.

jonathan: once staging smoke passes, can we tag v1 as registry-ready and flip the model-catalog entry? I can do the catalog PR.

maria: yes, please. I'll wait for the CI results and post back here with the final registry manifest. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
